s1.syndrome_frame: a cutaneous vascular lesion with telangiectasias in a patient with a history of rectal adenocarcinoma and metastases
salient_findings: a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque on the lower right lateral shin
discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels with superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels
key_facts: the patient is a man in his 40s
the patient has stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma
the patient has pulmonary and liver metastases
the patient has a history of radiation therapy and multiple chemotherapy cycles
the patient developed a cutaneous lesion in early January 2015
the lesion is a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque
the lesion is densely composed of telangiectasias
the lesion is not associated with pain or pruritus
the lesion grew to 4 cm
histopathological analysis showed discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels
genetic analysis identified a KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R somatic mutation

raw.rationale: The patient's cutaneous lesion is a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias, which is consistent with granuloma faciale. Histopathological analysis showed discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels, also supporting this diagnosis.

rejected.label: adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The cutaneous lesion does not appear to be a metastasis of the patient's rectal adenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: metastases
rejected.why: The lesion's characteristics do not suggest a metastatic lesion.

rejected.label: sarcoidosis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of granulomatous inflammation, which is typical of sarcoidosis.

rejected.label: vasculitis
rejected.why: The lesion is not associated with pain or pruritus, and histopathological analysis does not show inflammation of blood vessels, making vasculitis unlikely.
